title: Working Together Towards a Zero-suicide Singapore
what_it_is: Working Together Towards a Zero-suicide Singapore

sections.label: Global and Singapore teenage suicides
sections.summary: Nearly 800,000 people die by suicide yearly, and Singapore teenage suicides peaked in 2018, the highest since tracking began in 1991.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Close to 800,000 people lose their life to suicide every year, nearly one-third of which occur among young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here in Singapore, teenage suicides peaked in 2018 – the highest since suicide tracking started in 1991.

sections.label: Undetected attempts and Singapore rates
sections.summary: WHO estimates over 20 undetected suicide attempts per suicide, and Singapore's suicide rate stayed relatively unchanged from 9.5 per 100,000 in the 1980s to 8.3 today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, estimates from WHO show that for every suicide, there may have been more than 20 suicide attempts that go undetected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, whilst some may argue that our numbers are not high by international standards, we are still not doing enough because the number of deaths by suicides in Singapore has remained relatively unchanged from 9.5 suicides per 100,000 residents in the 1980s to 8.3 suicides per 100,000 residents today.

sections.label: Resources, funding and hospital tracking
sections.summary: The passage calls for identifying resources, more funding for suicide prevention and mental healthcare, and notes public hospitals do not track attempted-suicide admissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have failed so badly that I have no choice." This is the reality of suicides, and those who succumb can hardly be labelled as selfish.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This should first start from identifying currently available resources and committing further resources and funding to improve suicide prevention and efforts to support individuals struggling with suicide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should also consider increasing resources and funding for mental healthcare services to address wait time and patient load issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am deeply alarmed that our public hospitals do not track whether an admission is due to attempted suicide.

sections.label: Monitoring framework and teenage crisis
sections.summary: A monitoring and evaluation framework is required to instil accountability, and the spike in teenage suicides is described as a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A robust framework of monitoring and evaluation is also required, thereby instilling a sense of accountability among those in charge of interventions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have a crisis on our hands with the spike in teenage suicides.

sections.label: South Korea, Sweden and zero-suicide society
sections.summary: South Korea wants suicide-free communities and Sweden's 2008 Vision Zero Policy aims to prevent vulnerability-driven suicide, supporting a zero-suicide society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: South Korea wants to create safe and healthy communities free from suicide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And last but not least, Sweden’s Vision Zero Policy which was ratified by its parliament in 2008 aims to build a nation where no one should be in a situation of such vulnerability that suicide is seen as the only way out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we most certainly must not fail our people like Lucy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must work together towards a zero-suicide society that cares because every life matters.

sections.label: Singapore suicide rates and youth numbers
sections.summary: Singapore's 2016 age-standardised suicide rate of 7.9 per 100,000 was lower than South Korea, Japan, Finland and the US, while youth suicides fluctuated from 2014 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Internationally, based on WHO's 2016 age-standardised death rates, Singapore’s age-standardised death rates from suicide – 7.9 per 100,000 resident population – is lower compared to not just countries like South Korea at 20.2 and Japan 14.3, but also countries like Finland and US – 13.8, and 13.7 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the number of suicides involving 10- to 19-year-olds fluctuated from 13 cases in 2014, 27 in 2015, 22 in 2016, falling to 12 in 2017 and rising again to 22 in 2018.

sections.label: Attempted suicide decriminalised Singapore
sections.summary: As of 1 January 2020, attempted suicide is no longer a crime in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As of 1 January 2020, attempted suicide is no longer a crime in Singapore.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being
sections.summary: MOM intends to work with tripartite partners on a Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being, and TAFEP clarified companies should not ask applicants to declare mental health conditions unless job-related.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MOM has also announced their intention to work with tripartite partners to develop a Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In addition, the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) has recently clarified that companies should not ask for declaration of applicants’ mental health conditions unless there is a job-related requirement.

sections.label: Youth Mental Well-being network respondents
sections.summary: Since February this year, more than 800 people responded to Minister Desmond Lee's open call and will have an opportunity to be part of the Youth Mental Well-being network to be established.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since February this year, more than 800 people from different walks of life responded to Minister Desmond Lee’s open call and will have an opportunity to be part of the Youth Mental Well-being network to be established.
